note: Initial training-regime sweep: Windows (fixed/scaled/daily/wstride512) x Steps (150/600/2000). Warm-started from the global ckpt for every cell so the window/steps effect is isolated.

metadata.data_cleaning: dedup exact dups + clip recent 2520 trading days + mean-resolve (ticker,date) conflicts

metrics.MAPE: mean abs pct error of TTM forecast vs actual (scale-invariant, fund-comparable)
metrics.MAPE_pers: MAPE of naive persistence baseline (predict last known close flat)
metrics.dir_acc: percentage correct sign of mean change over the 96-step horizon
metrics.MAE: mean abs error in raw price (NOT comparable across tickers; NVR~$1000 vs AEP~$100)

results.flag: BUG: scaled-steps logic fired, ran only 20 steps; ignore
degenerate: 2 windows, overfit; dir_acc=50% worse than random

key_findings: TTM beats persistence baseline decisively: AEP 2.64% vs 8.54% MAPE; NVR 1.49% vs 8.80% at high2000. The model has real signal.
Direction accuracy 92-98% (vs 50% random) — strong for a fund's long/short timing.
Steps dominate: AEP MAPE 5.33->4.27->2.64 (150->600->2000); NVR 3.40->2.15->1.49. Diminishing but clear.
More data + proportional steps wins: scaled400@4000 (AEP 2.42, NVR 1.24) beats fixed200@2000 (AEP 2.64, NVR 1.49).
At FIXED steps, finer stride (more windows) is slightly WORSE (underfit: fewer epochs). Daily@600 (4.57) < fixed200@600 (4.27) for AEP.

wstride512 is degenerate: only 2 windows (512-context vs ~1294 closes), so it memorizes (MAPE 0.8 but dir_acc 50% = useless for a fund). Half-overlap with a 512 context on this data yields only 3 windows — overlap exploration only meaningful at stride<=64.
Batch in sweep=512 (not gd.BATCH=8); relative comparisons hold, but real backfill should revisit batch size.
All cells warm-started from the SAME global ckpt, so differences are window/steps effects only.
